text:
sqlpipe has three processes: a reader, a converter, and an uploader.

The reader connects to a Postgres database. It reads rows in batches. After it reads each batch, it sends the batch to the converter.

The converter receives a batch of rows. It converts the rows into a Parquet row group. A row group is a block of column-oriented data. The converter sends each completed row group to the uploader.

The uploader writes each row group to S3. It uses multipart upload. If a part fails, the uploader retries that part automatically. When all parts succeed, the uploader finalizes the object in S3.

The three processes run in a pipeline. Each process starts work as soon as data is available. This design keeps memory use low.
